name: Janez Janša
role: Prime Minister of the Republic of Slovenia (predsednik vlade Republike Slovenije)
party: Slovenska demokratska stranka (SDS) — European People's Party (EPP)
bio: Janez Janša (born Ivan Janša in 1958) has been Prime Minister of Slovenia since 4 June 2026, when his fourth government took office; the National Assembly had elected him on 22 May 2026 by 51 votes to 36. His Slovenian Democratic Party (SDS), which he has led since 1993, came second in the election of 22 March 2026 with 27.88% and 28 seats, one seat behind Robert Golob's Freedom Movement, and after Golob gave up on forming a government Janša built a coalition with New Slovenia, the Slovenian People's Party, Fokus and Anže Logar's Democrats (43 of 90 seats) with outside support from Resni.ca. A 1980s dissident convicted by a Yugoslav military court in the 1988 JBTZ trial and defence minister during the 1991 war of independence, he previously headed the government in 2004–2008 (euro adoption, Schengen entry, Slovenia's first EU Council presidency), in 2012–2013 (ended by a constructive vote of no confidence after an anti-corruption commission report on his assets) and in 2020–2022 (the COVID-19 pandemic, disputes with EU institutions over media freedom, the second EU presidency). His 2013 conviction in the Patria arms-procurement case, for which he spent 176 days in prison, was annulled by the Constitutional Court in 2015 before the case became time-barred; his acquittal in the Trenta property case became final in May 2026, while a 2022 conviction for insulting two journalists on Twitter is final. The 2026 campaign was overshadowed by secretly recorded videos that the intelligence agency SOVA linked to the Israeli private firm Black Cube; Janša confirmed meeting a Black Cube adviser and denies any involvement in the recordings. As of October 2026 his government has reversed its predecessor's measures against Israel, budgeted defence spending at 2.03% of GDP and passed the SKOK act on prosecuting corruption, while its tax-relief development act awaits a referendum on 6 December 2026 and voters rejected its amendment to the Parliamentary Inquiries Act on 11 October 2026.
